title: Rise of the Borderless Founder | Andreessen Horowitz
gist: a16z frames 'Borderless Founders' -- international founders who keep one foot in their home country and one in Silicon Valley -- as a distinct, underappreciated startup archetype, and describes a deliberate multi-year relationship-building playbook (dinners, repeat trips, diaspora bridging, cross-border customer intros) it runs to source and back these founders before the broader market notices them.

insights.claim: a16z defines 'Borderless Founders' as international founders who simultaneously build a Silicon Valley reputation and compound a network in their home country, gaining an underappreciated dual-network advantage over founders rooted in only one market.
insights.speaker: Gabriel Vasquez, Angela Strange
insights.so_what: Investors screening for talent-dense but overlooked founder pools should look at diaspora-connected founders with pre-existing home-market credibility, not just US-based first-time founders.

insights.claim: The authors argue that AI and remote work have collapsed physical distance to the point that Silicon Valley is now 'a state of mind rather than just a place,' so founders no longer must choose between their home network and the American market.
insights.speaker: Gabriel Vasquez, Angela Strange
insights.so_what: Signals a16z is deliberately investing in founders who keep HQ abroad rather than requiring US relocation -- a shift in what 'Silicon Valley company' means for deal sourcing.
insights.quote: Silicon Valley is now a state of mind rather than just a place—with AI and remote work collapsing physical distance

themes.theme: Preferential attachment as a startup growth mechanic

insights.claim: Marc Andreessen's preferential-attachment framework holds that startups enter a self-reinforcing loop where early resources (executives, financing, brand momentum, customers, government access) attract disproportionately more of the same resources, so the central strategic problem for a founder is how to get that loop started.
insights.speaker: Marc Andreessen (quoted by Gabriel Vasquez, Angela Strange)
insights.so_what: A useful diligence lens: assess whether a startup already shows early signs of compounding resource accrual (proof customers, notable hires, press) rather than static traction snapshots.
insights.quote: A startup needs to get into a loop where it’s accruing more and more resources as it goes… Economists call it preferential attachment.

insights.claim: a16z positions itself explicitly as a mechanism for jump-starting the preferential-attachment loop for Borderless Founders, acting as a 'bridge loan of power and momentum' before those founders have organically accrued enough resources to attract them on their own.
insights.speaker: Gabriel Vasquez, Angela Strange
insights.so_what: Explains a16z's rationale for investing relationship capital (dinners, intros, PR) ahead of traction -- a durable, hard-to-replicate sourcing moat versus funds that only chase visible momentum.
insights.quote: A16z was founded to give founders a bridge loan of power and momentum on their journey toward inevitability.

themes.theme: Three concrete advantages: customers, brand, talent

insights.claim: Pit, a Stockholm-based seed-stage AI platform startup founded by former Voi Mobility founder Adam Jaffer, landed H&M and Stena Metall as first customers largely on the strength of Jaffer's local reputation, despite not yet being globally known.
insights.speaker: Gabriel Vasquez, Angela Strange
insights.so_what: Local founder reputation can substitute for global brand recognition when landing enterprise design partners -- a signal to check a founder's home-market standing during diligence, not just Western press coverage.

insights.claim: Supersonik founder Daniel Carmona used a shared-university connection through the Spanish diaspora to reach Salesforce's CRO, converting that relationship into Salesforce becoming his first major enterprise contract.
insights.speaker: Gabriel Vasquez, Angela Strange
insights.so_what: Diaspora alumni networks can shortcut enterprise sales cycles at large US companies -- a repeatable go-to-market pattern for non-US founders targeting big-logo customers.
insights.locator: Supersonik founder Daniel Carmona had won global hackathons

insights.claim: The Polish government took a cap-table stake in ElevenLabs and opened an AI lab in Poland to inspire more AI companies among the country's 45,000 annual technical graduates, which in turn triggered a wave of international press coverage for ElevenLabs.
insights.speaker: Gabriel Vasquez, Angela Strange
insights.so_what: Government-as-investor/co-marketer is an emerging brand-acceleration channel for national-champion AI startups; watch for similar sovereign cap-table stakes as a signal of state-backed tech-sector promotion.
insights.locator: For ElevenLabs, the Polish government recently joined the cap table

insights.claim: Pit hired six technical leaders who had each previously served as CTO at a Swedish unicorn, tapping a pool of experienced repeat operators who were between ventures and ready to 're-enter the arena.'
insights.speaker: Gabriel Vasquez, Angela Strange
insights.so_what: Mature startup ecosystems (Sweden) generate a bench of proven ex-unicorn executives that early-stage founders with local ties can hire well below what a comparable US hire would cost or require.
insights.locator: Talent: This may be the most significant advantage of all

insights.claim: Segura, a Brazilian insurance-AI company, deliberately recruits from lesser-known university robotics teams rather than elite flagship programs, targeting highly motivated students the broader market has not yet identified.
insights.speaker: Gabriel Vasquez, Angela Strange
insights.so_what: Talent arbitrage in secondary university programs abroad is a lower-cost sourcing channel than competing for the same graduates as Silicon Valley incumbents.
insights.locator: Segura, an insurance AI company in Brazil

insights.claim: a16z systematically maps 'local luminary' founders in each country -- naming Sebas Mejia (Rappi), Guillermo Rauch (Vercel), Pedro Franceschi (Brex), Fredrik Hjelm (Voi) and Kristo Käärmann (Wise) -- and hosts curated dinners where these luminaries mentor next-generation founders, which doubles as a recruiting and branding channel for the luminaries' own companies.
insights.speaker: Gabriel Vasquez, Angela Strange
insights.so_what: This is a replicable, low-cost deal-sourcing structure -- track which VCs run similar 'repeat-founder-mentors-next-gen' dinner circuits as a proxy for pipeline quality in specific geographies.
insights.locator: Map the nodes from each country

insights.claim: In-person, repeated presence in home countries drove tangible government support: after Ben Horowitz hosted a Stockholm dinner with Swedish builders, the Swedish government granted ministerial access, trade-diplomacy inclusion, and regulatory-discussion participation to portfolio companies including Lovable and Legora, and Gabriel Vasquez personally flew to Sweden nine times in one year to sustain the relationship.
insights.speaker: Gabriel Vasquez, Angela Strange
insights.so_what: Sustained physical presence (not one-off trips) can convert into concrete state-level advantages (regulatory access, trade diplomacy) for portfolio companies -- a moat that's expensive for competitors to replicate quickly.
insights.quote: Consistent presence matters more than one-off trips. Gabe flew to Sweden nine times last year!
insights.locator: Go deep with the relationships that matter most

insights.claim: a16z's Borderless Founder dinner series has hosted over 600 founders and founding hires over five years, and its long-horizon approach paid off with attendees like Victor Cardenas, who attended a dinner three years before his company Slash reached unicorn status.
insights.speaker: Gabriel Vasquez, Angela Strange
insights.so_what: A multi-year, high-touch relationship funnel (600+ founders/5 years) is a quantifiable pipeline-building investment that predates visible traction -- useful benchmark for evaluating a fund's early-stage sourcing depth.
insights.locator: Our Borderless Founder dinner series has hosted 600+ founders

insights.claim: a16z builds relationships with promising individuals years before they become obviously valuable: Gabriel Vasquez began cultivating a relationship with Swedish student Gabriel Petersson long before Petersson joined OpenAI, eventually making him an a16z scout.
insights.speaker: Gabriel Vasquez, Angela Strange
insights.so_what: Early identification of unproven but well-referred individuals (via scout networks) is a way to get exposure to future high-value operators/founders before they're recognizable names.

insights.claim: a16z actively cross-introduces Borderless Founders to each other: it had backed Fernando Gadotti's second company at pre-seed and built a separate relationship with Sebastian Mejia while he was still at Rappi, then connected the two, leading them to co-found Tako, a Brazilian company targeting payroll and bureaucracy reduction.
insights.speaker: Gabriel Vasquez, Angela Strange
insights.so_what: VCs with deep, parallel founder relationships can manufacture co-founder matches and even new company formation -- a way funds create deal flow rather than just capture it.
insights.locator: Sometimes we introduce Borderless Founders to one another

insights.claim: a16z brokers cross-border customer relationships for portfolio companies: it connected ElevenLabs with TelevisaUnivision to dub its Spanish-language library while preserving actors' original intonation, which within months supported a follow-on agreement with Netflix, and separately introduced German-led company Factor to a large Latin American bank that became one of its first pilot customers.
insights.speaker: Gabriel Vasquez, Angela Strange
insights.so_what: Portfolio-to-portfolio and portfolio-to-corporate customer bridging across geographies is a concrete value-add VCs use to accelerate revenue -- worth probing for in any fund's stated 'platform support' claims.
insights.locator: We help our companies cross borders

insights.claim: a16z's New Media team provides portfolio companies a 'go-direct as a service' offering -- in-house creative, owned distribution channels (X, Substack, podcasts), a dedicated team, and AI-assisted network leverage -- which the authors say is especially effective for Borderless Founders whose stories are differentiated but undertold.
insights.speaker: Gabriel Vasquez, Angela Strange
insights.so_what: Media/brand infrastructure is being packaged as a standard VC platform service, not a one-off perk -- a differentiator to weigh when comparing term sheets from platform-heavy funds versus capital-only investors.
insights.locator: Brand: The a16z New Media team offers

insights.claim: a16z reports helping one portfolio company transition from founder-led to scalable sales, tripling its top-of-funnel and increasing ARR by 70% within a few months.
insights.speaker: Gabriel Vasquez, Angela Strange
insights.so_what: A concrete (if single-anecdote, unnamed-company) ARR-growth claim tied to VC operational support; treat as illustrative rather than statistically representative given no company name or sample size is given.
insights.quote: One company tripled its top-of-funnel and increased ARR by 70% in just a few months through our network.
insights.locator: Talent: While Borderless Founders start with strong networks

insights.claim: More than half of America's billion-dollar (unicorn) companies were founded or co-founded by immigrants, according to the authors.
insights.speaker: Gabriel Vasquez, Angela Strange
insights.so_what: Reinforces immigrant/international founders as a disproportionately high-value cohort for venture returns -- a base-rate argument for weighting sourcing toward diaspora and international-founder networks.
insights.quote: More than half of America’s billion-dollar companies were founded or co-founded by immigrants.

insights.claim: 44% of a16z Apps' investments over the past two years feature international founders, split evenly between companies headquartered in the US and abroad -- indicating the firm has already shifted a large share of its capital toward this founder profile rather than treating it as a niche.
insights.speaker: Gabriel Vasquez, Angela Strange
insights.so_what: A direct disclosure of portfolio composition: nearly half of a major fund's app-layer bets are international-founder-led, a signal for LPs and co-investors about where a16z Apps sees return potential concentrating.
insights.quote: 44% of investments made by a16z Apps in the last two years feature international founders, split evenly between HQ in the US and abroad
